title: Parallel execution and splitting the suite

videos.script: A suite that takes ten minutes gets run less often. And a suite that is run less often finds its defects later. {{clock}} So this lesson makes the suite faster, in two ways. The first is on one machine. Playwright starts several workers, each a process with its own browser, and hands them files to run at the same time. {{workers}} You time the whole suite with one worker, then two, then four, on a laptop with four processors. {{timings}} Then something goes red. The shop keeps one basket for everybody, and four workers fill it at once. You read which tests collided, and why a reset at the start does not save them. {{collision}} The tests that share the shop get a single worker of their own, and the rest keep running in parallel. {{projects}} The second way is across machines. A shard is a slice of the suite, and three machines can each run one. You see how Playwright cuts the slices, and why one long file makes one long slice. {{shards}} Last, the cost. Every worker is a browser, and a browser needs memory and processor time. Past the number of processors, more workers stop helping. You measure where that happens. {{cost}}
